newsitem.title: USA: Coke to launch new worldwide ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Coke to launch new worldwide ad campaign.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co. on Monday introduced a new worldwide advertising campaign, which features sumo wrestlers, bagpipes, a Shakespeare parody and the familiar tagline "Always Coca-Cola."

The 16 new commercials use a variety of production techniques -- from animation to computer-generated special effects to live action -- to reach a broad consumer market, said Sergio Zyman, Coca-Cola's chief marketing officer.

The new commercials showcase Coca-Cola's classic, contour-shaped glass bottle and a wide range of locations, music and subjects. The commercials aim to project both the familiar appeal and the international reach of Coca-Cola, Zyman said.
"We must use our ads, our packaging, our marketing to communicate 'Coca-Cola-ness' to all ... all the time," Zyman said at a screening for reporters in Manhattan.
The ads begin airing in mid-May and continue the "Always Coca-Cola" campaign theme, which started in 1993.
Edge Creative of Los Angeles created 15 of the ads and Leo Burnett Inc. of Chicago created one.

In one ad parodying Shakespeare's King Lear, the King is ready to divest his throne to a daughter who professes the greatest love for him. His first two daughters speak of love and loyalty, but the last daughter, in the greatest show of love, offers a supply of ice cold Coca-Cola.

"The connection between the consumers and the brand happens instantly when you see the shape of the contour bottle. But that connection also takes place on the beach or at the ballpark. It can be something whimsical or something awe-inspiring," Zyman said.
The company declined to disclose its 1997 advertising and marketing budget. But Zyman said "there's not a market around the world where we are spending less.
"If we want daily consumption, we need daily advertising," he said.

Coca-Cola said it will bolster its advertising spending in Mexico, the United Kingdom, Japan, Argentina and South Africa. The United States, however, remains the toughest and most competitive market, Zyman said.
The ads are just part of Coca-Cola's global marketing effort, which also includes sponsorships and promotions.
"We believe very strongly that the old way of marketing is dead. We know that eerything we say and do communicates. And for that matter, everything we don't say and don't do communicates.
"Marketing is a lot more than advertising. Advertising is a part, but it can be a small part.
Coca-Cola said its volume has increased 21 percent in the last three years. The company declined to provide specific sales or growth goals.
